title: Genetic transformation of Aureobasidium pullulans via Agrobacterium tumefaciens-mediated transformation
author: Julian Liber

steps.title: Electroporate plasmid into AGL1
steps.instruction: Transform the binary plasmid that replicates in A. tumefaciens and expresses in A. pullulans into Agrobacterium strain AGL1 by electroporation using the Addgene vector (see https://dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.g8ubzww).

steps.title: Plate resuspended Agrobacterium cells
steps.instruction: Without diluting, plate 20 µL of the resuspended electroporated cells onto appropriate selective medium, tilt the plate to create a drip, and incubate for 48 h at 28 °C.

steps.title: Inoculate Agrobacterium in LM+
steps.instruction: In a 50 mL tube, add a streak of colonies from the electroporation‑transformed cells and inoculate 5 mL of LM+ medium containing 15 µg/mL rifampicin.

steps.title: Inoculate yeast line in YPD
steps.instruction: In a separate 50 mL tube, inoculate 5 mL of YPD with the Aureobasidium pullulans line intended for transformation.

steps.title: Induce Agrobacterium culture
steps.instruction: Grow the Agrobacterium culture to induction stage: pellet cells by centrifugation at 3000 × g (temperature not specified) for 10 min, discard supernatant, resuspend in 5 mL of 1× IM, vortex, then incubate at 230 rpm, 28 °C for 4–6 h.

substeps.instruction: Replace supernatant with 5 mL 1× IM and vortex

steps.title: Prepare yeast suspension at OD0.25
steps.instruction: When Agrobacterium cells are nearly ready, process the yeast culture: centrifuge 1.5–2 mL of yeast in a microcentrifuge tube at 15000 × g (temperature not specified) for 30 s, discard supernatant, resuspend in 1 mL water, centrifuge again, discard supernatant, finally suspend the pellet in 300 µL water; measure OD600 and dilute to 0.25 (you will need 50 µL of this suspension per transformation).

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge 1.5–2 mL yeast at 15000 × g for 30 s
Discard supernatant and resuspend pellet in 1 mL water
Resuspend final pellet in 300 µL water

steps.title: Create divots in IM plates
steps.instruction: Flame‑sterilize a glass test tube, allow it to cool in a sterile environment, and use it to press four divots distributed in quadrants on the IM plates.

steps.title: Add yeast‑Agrobacterium mixture to divots
steps.instruction: Mix 50 µL of the 0.25 OD600 yeast suspension with 50 µL of the induced Agrobacterium culture, then pipette the entire 100 µL mixture into each divot on the plate.

steps.title: Dry and incubate co‑culture plates
steps.instruction: Leave the plates on the bench with lids on to dry overnight, then place them in a 24 °C incubator inside a sealed bag or wrapped in parafilm; incubate for at least 3 days (ideally 5) until a lawn of colonies appears in each divot.

steps.title: Streak co‑culture onto selective YPD
steps.instruction: Using a sterile wood streaker, collect as much co‑culture as possible from each divot, transfer to one quadrant of a square YPD plate containing the appropriate antibiotics, draw a line at the edge of the quadrant, and streak back‑and‑forth progressively away from the line to create a dilution gradient.

steps.title: Incubate and select fluorescent colonies
steps.instruction: Incubate the streak plate at 28 °C until colonies become visible and fluorescence can be detected; promptly transfer selected colonies to a fresh plate before PCR genotyping to avoid false positives from residual bacteria.
